audit.reason: Three additions decided on 2026-10-11. (1) The form of the engagement as its own datum: On-Going ratio 1 and On-Demand ratio 1.10 on price, one record per form instead of a second set of pricing policies. (2) Start-up provisions costed instead of the workbook rule of one month of the resource: account onboarding (USD 200, once per person, default) and recruiting (USD 500, optional, only when a person has to be hired); both estimates proposed by the agent and accepted by the CEO; the USD 100 test placeholder stops being selected. (3) CLP to USD at the inverse of the quote FX, so a cost invoiced in CLP can be carried in its own currency. Pricing policies and floors are untouched.

record.note: On-Going engagement: the reference form, no premium (price ratio 1). Commercial-model multiplier of the pricing workbook, kept on 2026-10-11. General record: it applies to every offer without a record of its own.

On-Demand engagement: +10% on the price of every row (price ratio 1.10). It is the commercial-model multiplier of the pricing workbook. On 2026-10-11 the CEO asked whether 10% was right and left any adjustment to the agent, who kept it: it sits at the low end of the 10-15% that agencies discount a retainer against a project rate, and in V3 start-up, coordination and supplier commitments are costed apart instead of hiding in the premium. General record: it applies to every offer without a record of its own.

Start-up provision charged once for each person who joins an account: accesses, brief and brand immersion. Proposed by the agent and accepted by the CEO on 2026-10-11. Basis: about two days of the lead's time, from the catalog cost of the Creative Operations Lead profile (ECG-001, USD 1,900 a month); the figure is the accepted round amount, not a measurement. Estimated: to be measured on the next two real incorporations and then replaced. It replaces the placeholder trial-setup. The workbook rule of one month of the resource's cost as recruiting and onboarding fee is not carried into the quoter; the protection it sought belongs to the contract terms (minimum term, conversion clause).
